The quashing of criminal proceedings in an offence under Section 307 IPC came up for detailed
discussion before the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Narinder Singh and others vs. After due consideration the Hon'ble Apex Court formalised the
issue of compounding of offences under Section 307 IPC to say that it is an offence against society
and is non-compoundable, but in certain cases the High Court would be guided to give adequate
treatment to the settlement between the parties in exercise of inherent powers under Section 482
Cr.P.C. (V) While exercising its powers, the High Court is to examine as to whether the possibility of
conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of criminal cases would put the accused to great

open to the High Court to examine as to whether incorporation of Section 307 IPC is there for the
sake of it or the prosecution has collected sufficient evidence, which if proved, would lead to proving
the charge under Section 307 IPC. For this purpose, it would be open to the High Court to go by the
nature of injury sustained, whether such injury is inflicted on the vital/delegate parts of the body,
nature of weapons used etc.

260 IN THE HIGH COURT OF PUNJAB AND HARYANA
AT CHANDIGARH
CRM-M No. The extent and sweep of inherent
powers of the High Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C., for quashing criminal prosecution on merits as
well as on the basis of compromise between the accused and the victim remained question of
interpretation since long. The Hon'ble Apex Court after due 2 of 19 consideration of judgments in
Madhu Limaye vs. The legal
position summed up in the said judgment is in the following manner:-
"Thus, the law is that Article 227 of the Constitution of India gives the High Court the
power of superintendence over all courts and tribunals throughout the territories in
relation to which it exercises jurisdiction. However, the power under Article 227 is a discretionary power
and it is difficult to attribute to an order of the High Court, such a source of power, when the High
Court itself does not in terms purport to exercise any such discretionary power. It is settled law that
this power of judicial superintendence, under Article 227, must be exercised sparingly and only to
keep subordinate courts and tribunals within the bound of their authority and not to correct mere
errors. Thus the
inherent jurisdiction of the High Court under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code can be
exercised even when 4 of 19 there is a bar under Section 397 or some other provisions of the
Criminal Procedure Code. If the order assailed is purely
of an interlocutory character, which could be corrected in exercise of revisional powers or appellate
powers the High Court must refuse to exercise its inherent power. The inherent power is to be used
only in cases where there is an abuse of the process of the Court or where interference is absolutely
necessary for securing the ends of justice. Full Bench of this Court in Kulwinder Singh and others vs. There is no statutory bar which can affect the inherent powers of High Court under Section
482 Cr.P.C. The powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C., is to be exercised Ex-Debitia, justitia to prevent
abuse of process of Court.

court and the matter is at the appellate stage before the High Court, mere compromise between the

already been convicted by the trial court. {10}. In view of aforesaid, there cannot be any strong possibility of
conviction of the accused persons. {11}. {12}. Consequently, this criminal petition is allowed. FIR No. 65 dated 05.05.2016 registered under
